- Overestimate prices during sentiment spikes (especially +0.67 or 1.00) — reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to recent highs.
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment (e.g., -0.67 or 0.00) — add 1–3% to forecast to avoid mean reversion underestimation.
- Overshoot after recent price spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below the immediate prior peak.
- Lagged forecasts (especially 30d) tend to overreact to sentiment — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for sentiment >0.67.
- When sentiment is neutral or low (0.33 or 0.00), forecast should be closer to 30d moving average — avoid sharp directional moves.
- Avoid overconfidence in early forecast days — reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% if sentiment is mixed or weak.
